title: Отказ Нагиева и приглашение Елены  (Nagiyev's Refusal and Inviting Elena)

segments.t: In the office, Nagiyev thinks Max is joking when the young cook asks to borrow money and sends him away empty-handed. Back in the kitchen, Chef Barinov calls Elena Pavlovna to announce that the apartment is completely free for the evening.
Елена Павловна, у меня мама на балет ушла.
Let's replay the exchange and look closely at each Russian phrase.
'I do not understand.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'not' and finishing on 'understood?'.
'In that sense?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'that' and finishing on 'sense'. Elena answers right away.
'For sheer nerve.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'behind' before landing on 'nerve'.
'What is with you?' The grammar packs 'you' and 'what' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'I was only joking.' The '-l' ending on the verb meaning 'joked' places the action in the masculine past tense. Kostya answers right away.
'Does he know how to talk?' The grammar packs 'to talk' and 'knows how' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Stepan Andreyevich?' Elena brings out the contrast between 'Stepan' and 'andreyevich' in a few short words.
Елена Павловна, у меня мама на балет ушла.
'Elena Pavlovna, my mother has gone out to the ballet.' Kostya brings out the contrast between 'Elena' and 'Pavlovna' in a few short words. Elena answers right away.
'Why walk on foot?' In Russian, the idea of 'why' flows naturally into 'on foot' without extra filler words.
'What I meant to say was...' The '-l' ending on the verb meaning 'wanted' places the action in the masculine past tense.
'Really? Sounds good?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'yes' and finishing on 'fine'. Kostya answers right away.
'Well then, what do you say?' The meaning hinges on 'come on' working together with 'what' in spoken Russian.
'See you soon.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'until' and finishing on 'meeting'. Let's hear the complete conversation once more.
Елена Павловна, у меня мама на балет ушла.
